title: Tenant rules on every tenant model, added beside today's group rules (stage 1, additive)
description:
Outcome: Every tenant-owned model gets rules that grant an operation only to a session whose role claim names the row's tenant, in the form proven by the spike. Today's rules (allow.groups(contentWriteGroups), allow.group("editor"), allow.groups(categoryWriteGroups), allow.group(adminGroup)) stay, so nothing changes for anyone yet; this release only makes the tenant rules exist and testable. tenantId becomes immutable after create (field-level rule or resolver check, as the spike found). Identity models that span sites (UserProfile, UserIdentity, PublicHandleClaim) are not tenant models and keep owner/admin rules.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): amplify/data/schema.ts (46 models in buildBaseDefinitions), amplify/functions/editorial-checks/schema.ts (EditorialPolicy, EditorialCheckSettings, EditorialFeedback, EditorialCheckRun), amplify/functions/proposal-actions/schema.ts (Proposal), amplify/plugins/reader-steering/schema.ts (8 Reader* and ModerationAction models, staff rules), amplify/plugins/signup/schema.ts (SignupEntry), scripts/test-schema-parity.ts.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-rules-additive.feature):
Scenario: The tenant rule admits the right tenant's editor
    Given an editor session acting for "alpha" with no Cognito group
    When it reads and updates an "alpha" Item
    Then both succeed

Scenario: Group members keep today's access during stage 1
    Given a dedicated site whose editors are in the "editor" group
    When an editor saves a story
    Then it succeeds exactly as before

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-9f3de0, PPY-0bb0fd, PPY-94d609. Blocks PPY-baa75d, PPY-bdc4ee, PPY-13fbea. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-5e0259.

Testing: Schema parity test lists every rule; Behave against a sandbox with both rule kinds; the adversarial suite (PPY-29f730) starts running here in report-only mode.
Rollout: One release for every site (rules are not indexes, so no staging by table). No behaviour change because the group rules still grant.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: Amplify rules are OR-ed, so stage 1 gives no isolation at all; someone may believe it does. Mitigation: the feature file and the release note say so; isolation is claimed only after PPY-bdc4ee.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: changes: adds tenant rules to the 57 tenant models (additive).
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
